title: Week 11 Overview: Lists and Dictionaries, Continued
body:
Week 11 Overview: Lists and Dictionaries, Continued (Delivery Week)

Week at a glance

Monday (Oct 26): Monday Moments, AI I Lens 11: Verify. How do we know whether an AI answer is trustworthy? Checking a program that processes a collection against edge cases, such as an empty list or duplicate keys, is the programming form of verifying a claim.

Wednesday (Oct 28): Wacky Wednesday, Professional Minds Week 11: how do projects become reliable products?

Friday (Oct 30): Fun Friday. Share the edge cases your collections program was tested against.

This week's focus

Dictionaries, and the choice between a dictionary and a list. When you look things up by a name or an ID, a dictionary replaces searching by hand. Build the lookup from your world's real data, not from a hardcoded literal.

This week's gate

The week-11 Odyssey gate is "The registry, and the first real trade-off". Add a dictionary that looks up an entity from Week 10's list by name or ID, and show at least one lookup returning a real result. The gate also asks for your first Decide/Compare: commit in writing to your data-structure choice first, then compare it against at least one real alternative, naming a trade-off that is specific to your world's data.

The due date and time are shown on the assignment in Canvas. A bonus practice assignment is also available this week and is optional.

Optional reading and listening

For a second explanation of dictionaries, read Chapter 9 of Python for Everybody by Charles R. Severance, which is free to read online, or listen to it here: audio of Chapter 9: Dictionaries (about 17 minutes). Reading and audio are optional.
